headline: Oklahoma's only big-league team: sell its clay and sky in Thunder blue, statewide and under $100.
thesis: Apart from the Hornets' 2005-07 Katrina stay, the Thunder are the only big-league team Oklahoma has had, so the market is the whole state: Tulsa, Norman, Lawton, Stillwater, tribal nations and small-town gyms. Thunder blue is the one color a split Sooner-and-Cowboy household can share, and that rule should govern everything, including the City Edition. The fanbase is a 2025 champion with back-to-back MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, stung by a seven-game West finals loss to San Antonio and proud of a roster Sam Presti drafted and developed. Nike wins with a deep, sub-$100 'Oklahoma' layer in big-box and mall doors statewide, a few credited, paid artist drops from the Plaza, Paseo, Deep Deuce and Tulsa, and a blue-bodied 2027-28 City Edition that reads 'Oklahoma' across the chest.

archetype.name: The One-Team State
archetype.description: A whole state that adopted a franchise in 2008 and now wears a champion as its civic uniform. Loud, loyal, value-minded and allergic to flash the team has not earned.

pulse.teamMoment: Back-to-back MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's Thunder went 64-18 and are 2026-27 co-title favorites (BetMGM win total 60.5, the West's highest) after San Antonio beat them 4-3 in the West finals. Luguentz Dort went to Atlanta, Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins were also traded, Aday Mara (No. 12), Bennett Stirtz and Otega Oweh were drafted, and Presti won't cut a payroll near $260M.
pulse.sentiment: Confident but stung. Fans expect a title, see the Oct 20 opener at San Antonio as a grudge match, and trust Presti and Mark Daigneault's patient build even as familiar rotation players leave.

topInsights.title: The market is Oklahoma, not OKC
topInsights.insight: With no NFL, MLB or NHL team in the state, Thunder fans drive in from Tulsa, Lawton, Norman and Stillwater and buy at big-box and mall doors along I-35, I-40 and the Turner Turnpike. The state outline and the word 'Oklahoma' travel everywhere; 405 means the OKC metro, while Tulsa is 918 and the west and south are 580.
topInsights.implication: Lead the statewide layer with the state outline and an 'Oklahoma' wordmark, sell 405, 918 and 580 as a matched area-code set aimed door by door, and give Tulsa (Utica Square, Woodland Hills) its own allocation.

topInsights.title: Thunder blue is the peace treaty in a Sooner-and-Cowboy house
topInsights.insight: Fall closets are OU crimson and OSU orange, many households are split between them, and everyone is Thunder. Orange-heavy or crimson-leaning blocking reads as a college allegiance, and a burnt-orange body also reads as Texas.
topInsights.implication: Every Thunder piece, the City Edition included, is blue-bodied with Sunset (#EF3B24) and red-clay rust as trim; launch midweek or on Thunder Cup Fridays, never on football Saturdays.

topInsights.title: Red Dirt is a Stillwater sound and a Stockyards wardrobe
topInsights.insight: Red Dirt music grew out of Stillwater's songwriter scene (Turnpike Troubadours and John Moreland carry it now), and its look lives in gig posters for rooms like Tulsa's Cain's Ballroom and in Stockyards City stores like Langston's. The clay itself stains every sneaker in the state.
topInsights.implication: A rust (#A8442A) and canvas capsule with gig-poster lettering by a commissioned Oklahoma poster artist, launched through a Red Dirt-booked show and always sold next to a hoops-first blue line so the Thunder never read as a country brand.

topInsights.title: Own the sky through Oklahoma landmarks, not gradients
topInsights.insight: Storm fronts and sunsets are real here, but a sky gradient alone passes for Kansas City or Denver, and the Thunder palette is already a sunset. What only Oklahoma has is the Skydance Bridge's scissortail sail over I-40, the Deco rooflines of downtown Tulsa and OKC, and the flat sky-blue field of the state flag.
topInsights.implication: Use the Skydance sail line and stepped Deco silhouettes as the signature graphics, keep packable shells core from October to April, and hold any gradient headline until the earlier City Editions are checked; never use tornado-damage or memorial imagery.

topInsights.title: Built here: the fan pride is development, and SGA is the style story
topInsights.insight: Fans are proudest of a core Presti drafted and developed (Williams, Holmgren, now Mara) and of Loud City at Paycom Center, not of a victory lap. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, a Hamilton, Ontario native, is also one of the league's most-watched tunnel dressers, with a Canadian following of his own.
topInsights.implication: Write opener and season copy around development and Loud City rather than avenging a loss, keep any 2025 champion reference to licensed marks, and add an SGA tunnel-fit story once the brand and licensing path for his product is confirmed.

topInsights.title: Value-minded ritual buyers with a hard $100 line
topInsights.insight: Oklahomans buy in person at Penn Square, Academy, Dick's, Hibbett, the arena store and the Nike Factory Store at OKC Outlets on I-40. An August sales-tax holiday on clothing and shoes under $100 lands on school start, and Nike has no community or flagship door in town.
topInsights.implication: Price a full Thunder ladder (tees, shorts, hoodies, youth footwear) at $99 or less with deep youth sizes, and use borrowed venues (arena, Plaza and Midtown pop-ups, local gyms) for storytelling.

topInsights.title: The richest stories belong to specific communities
topInsights.insight: The state's deepest design sources are dozens of sovereign Native nations, Deep Deuce jazz and Clara Luper's 1958 sit-ins, Tulsa's Greenwood and Black Wall Street, the Classen Asian District, Southside car culture and the NW 39th Gayborhood. None of them is a theme to borrow, and even names like 'Red Earth' already belong to a Native institution.
topInsights.implication: Any piece drawing on these communities starts with a named partner who sets terms, approves the work, is credited and paid, and launches it at a community event; no regalia, sacred imagery, scripts or memorial imagery.

collection.name: Clay & Sky
collection.story: Oklahoma is red clay underfoot and a huge sky overhead, and Thunder blue holds the two together. The collection runs from Stockyards work-wear to the Skydance Bridge sail line, with a statewide value layer any family can afford and limited pieces by local artists.

uniform.narrative: Every Oklahoman knows the line where red clay meets a storm sky; this set puts it on a Dark Blue jersey with a rust horizon band and 'Oklahoma' across the chest, drawn by Oklahoma sign painters. It targets 2027-28, since the 2026-27 set is not yet confirmed, and gives a state whose last City Edition was a recolor an original story to collect.
motifs: A rust horizon band across the chest and yoke, with clay below and Dark Blue sky above
The Skydance Bridge sail line on the side panels
Stepped Art Deco geometry from downtown Tulsa and OKC
Directional wind lines in place of lightning bolts
Hand-painted ghost-sign texture inside the numbers
uniform.typography: An original 'Oklahoma' chest wordmark (the Utah Jazz and Indiana Pacers set the state-name precedent) in Route 66 and Automobile Alley showroom lettering, hand-drawn by a commissioned Oklahoma sign painter; outlined slab numbers in Yellow with a rust keyline. Get the league's read on the wordmark at concept stage.

partners.name: Plaza District Association

partners.name: Jabee
partners.why: Long-time voice of Northeast OKC hip-hop and the Black creative scene.
partners.idea: Co-curate the Deep Deuce and Northeast OKC release and its artists for Juneteenth 2027, with proceeds directed by community partners.

partners.name: Greenwood Cultural Center
partners.type: Tulsa Black history and cultural institution
partners.why: The long-standing keeper of Greenwood and Black Wall Street history, and the right first call before Nike shows up in North Tulsa.
partners.idea: Advise on whether and how the Booker T. Washington program and any Tulsa activation happen, on paid, credited terms.

partners.name: First Americans Museum
partners.why: A civic institution that can make introductions but cannot speak for any sovereign nation.
partners.idea: Introductions only, leading to direct agreements with a named nation's cultural or commerce office for the November 2027 program.

partners.name: Yatika Starr Fields
partners.type: Oklahoma muralist and painter (Cherokee, Osage and Muscogee)
partners.why: Internationally exhibited Oklahoma muralist with bold, color-saturated work.
partners.idea: His own paid commission on his own terms, such as a mural or artist piece, not a stand-in for any nation.

partners.name: Jeff Chanchaleune (Ma Der Lao Kitchen, Bar Sen)
partners.why: James Beard-recognized chef whose Plaza District restaurants made Lao food an OKC story.
partners.idea: Food pairing at Plaza releases and introductions to Lao community artists, not the Asian District anchor.

partners.name: Oklahoma Contemporary Arts Center
partners.why: The state's leading contemporary art venue with studios and a Midtown campus.
partners.idea: Run the open call that selects District Series artists and the City Edition sign painter.

partners.name: Shop Good

partners.idea: Stock the Red Dirt capsule and District Series as the tastemaker door Nike lacks in OKC.

risks.risk: Roster churn on a payroll near $260M, and player product that runs through other licensing paths: SGA's shoe deal is with Converse and name-and-number items need NBPA group licensing.
risks.mitigation: Limit names to SGA, Williams and Holmgren in licensed formats, confirm the brand path for SGA product, keep most product team-first, and hold Mara items until his role is clear.

risks.risk: Lead times: new NBA-licensed product takes months, and product built for a deep run sits unsold if the playoffs end early.
risks.mitigation: Use in-line product for October 2026, put every new line on a spring or August 2027 date, and print round product to demand.

risks.risk: Native appropriation, such as borrowing the 'Red Earth' name, selling on Statehood Day (the end of Indian Territory) or treating one artist or museum as speaking for nations.
risks.mitigation: No Statehood Day hooks; Native work only under a named nation's written terms, pay and approval through N7; Red Earth supported only as a paid, credited partner.

risks.risk: Showing up in Tulsa near Greenwood without a local Black partner, or using Black Wall Street or 1921 massacre imagery.
risks.mitigation: No Greenwood, Black Wall Street or massacre imagery, and no Tulsa activations near May 31 or Juneteenth unless the Greenwood Cultural Center or another named Tulsa Black partner leads.

risks.risk: Thunder product reads as OU crimson, OSU orange or Texas burnt orange and loses half of a split-loyalty household.
risks.mitigation: Blue-bodied palettes, rust and Sunset as trim, and fan-panel color reviews in OKC and Tulsa against college gear before launch.

scorecard.rationale: A champion that is the only big-league team in an entire state gives OKC near-top fan intensity and a large statewide opportunity for a small metro, with distinct red-dirt, Skydance, Route 66 and community stories to design from. Retail lags: a car-based, value-minded market with no Nike community door and a small sneaker scene.
